summary.headline: Maan Aluminium Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR232 crore and EBITDA to INR7 crore, with margin near 3%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR232 crore, up 10% YoY from INR211 crore but down from INR255 crore in Q4 FY26. EBITDA rose to INR7 crore from INR5 crore sequentially, with margin about 3% versus about 2%, and PAT was about INR3 crore (EPS INR0.52 vs INR0.29). Management said exports fell to about 45% of manufacturing revenue (from 60-70% earlier) due to duties, and freight and Middle East shipping disruption continue to weigh on volumes and costs. Capex of about INR166 crore over three years is planned, with Dewas precision tubing and Pithampur Italian press ramp-up the key near-term items.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Q1 manufacturing turnover above INR70 crore with about 40% exports (management also cited ~45% export share of manufacturing revenue in prepared remarks). Production about 1,558 MT against 24,000 MT extrusion capacity. Anodizing utilisation ~45-50% and machining ~55%.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Described as opportunistic and pass-through; the remainder of the INR232 crore revenue (about INR160 crore implied) comes from trading. Management expects trading to decline as manufacturing mix rises.

guidance_outlook: Volumes expected to stay flattish QoQ and for FY27; ramp-up possibly toward end of FY27 or start of FY28.
Manufacturing revenue guided flattish; management would be 'okay' with FY26 level of ~INR300 crore manufacturing top line.
Pithampur Italian press: management targets ~35%/50%/75% ramp in a three-year plan; currently ~25% ramp-up; significant contribution expected by mid-FY28.
Dewas aluminium precision tubing plant: online targeted within 6-8 months, before mid-FY28 (no firm date given); capex mostly in H2 FY27.
Recovery of gas/energy cost increases: about 50% passed to customers over last two quarters, balance expected to be recovered in one to two quarters as contracts renew.
Management said no new debt planned for capex; company is deleveraging and has sufficient cash. Employee expenses expected not to rise materially as technical team is already hired.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity: foundry 12,000 TPA; extrusion 24,000 TPA; anodizing 3,600 TPA; machining 1,400 TPA.
Three-year capex plan of ~INR166 crore cumulative, including Pithampur, new dials and general capex, and new plants under development; ~INR90 crore allocated to new plants.
Dewas precision tubing project: total capex ~INR45 crore, of which ~INR15-20 crore spent to date; aimed at aerospace, defence and automotive; expected asset turn at least 2-3x at peak utilisation.
Capex spend in Q1 FY27 was less than INR5 crore; overseas visit planned to finalise extrusion press and other machinery for Dewas; majority of capex in H2 FY27.
Pithampur capacity was expanded from 1,200 MT to 12,000-24,000 MT near end of last year; Italian press now online.
demand_pricing: Export share has dropped from around 60-70% to about 45% (about 40% in Q1 per call Q&A) because of duties hitting the export business; management aims to shift volume to domestic high-value business, which is slow to convert.
Freight rates up 5-10x on Strait of Hormuz and Middle East disruption; customers in GCC and East Asia holding back orders; delays and backed-up shipping persist.
Conversion margins: plain extrusion 6-10% (management cited 6-8% and 6-10%); value-added processing (powder coating, machining, anodizing) targeted at 15%+.
Commodity exposure: most manufacturing volumes hedged via LME/MCX on order basis; unhedged positions kept under 5%; management says commodity moves impact margins by less than 5%.

Trading is a pass-through business at metal prices; management said EBITDA per ton is reported on a blended basis only, with manufacturing EBITDA per ton not readily available (last quarter's USD340/ton reference not updated).

qa_highlights.question: What was the capacity volume this quarter and EBITDA per ton (last quarter USD340/t)?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA is reported only on a blended basis; manufacturing per-ton figure not available. Total extrusion production was about 1,558 MT in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any ramp-up in volumes sooner than expected?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management reiterated flattish volumes, with any ramp-up toward end FY27 or early FY28. The export loss from duties is being replaced by slow-converting domestic business.

qa_highlights.question: How are aluminium prices hedged and how do margins change with value addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedging is order-linked on LME/MCX, with under 5% unhedged; plain extrusion margins are 6-10%, rising to 15%+ with value addition. Management said absolute EBITDA per ton is the right metric for conversion.

qa_highlights.question: Dewas project status, timing and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR15-20 crore of INR45 crore spent; online targeted within 6-8 months, before mid-FY28, with no firm date. Asset turn at least 2-3x; no margin figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company take on debt for capex, and how will employee costs move?
qa_highlights.answer: No debt planned; management said the company is deleveraging. Employee costs are not expected to rise materially as the technical team is already on payroll.

qa_highlights.question: How has other expenses fallen and how are energy costs being recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses fell from INR18 crore to INR13 crore over four quarters. About 50% of the gas cost increase was passed to customers, with the rest to follow as contracts renew.

financial_highlights.change: +10% YoY (vs INR211 crore); -9% QoQ (vs INR255 crore in Q4 FY26)
~+40% QoQ (vs INR5 crore in Q4 FY26)
vs INR2 crore in Q4 FY26
vs INR810 crore in FY25, broadly flat

risks_watch: Export share fell from about 60-70% to about 45% (about 40% in Q1) due to duties; domestic high-value replacement business is slow to convert.
Freight rates up 5-10x amid Strait of Hormuz and Middle East disruption; GCC and East Asia customers holding orders, with delays and backed-up shipping persisting.

Dewas aluminium precision tubing plant (about INR45 crore capex, about INR15-20 crore spent) has no firm commissioning date; management declined to commit beyond 'next year'. Most capex falls in H2 FY27.
Pithampur Italian press at about 25% ramp-up versus a 35%/50%/75% three-year plan; management expects significant contribution only by mid-FY28.

Working capital cycle elongated from FY25 to FY26 due to raw material procurement and customer credit; gas/energy cost pass-through only about 50% recovered so far, balance tied to contract renewals over the next one to two quarters.
Manufacturing EBITDA per ton not disclosed (only blended), so the earlier USD340/t reference cannot be tracked.
key_quotes: So, the freight rates are still quite high.
I cannot honestly because I've done that in the past that I'm sure you're aware planning and dates in India they go -- they always go ahead.

So we are happy that we've achieved a 25% sort of ramp-up, but still a lot of tooling, still a lot of development still happening, a lot of aerospace grade alloys and defense grade alloys, we are working towards special automotive sector alloys.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on strategy and balance sheet (no new debt, deleveraging) but cautious on near-term volumes, guiding flattish and deferring ramp-up to late FY27 or early FY28. It was evasive on specifics: it declined to give Dewas dates, margins, asset turn beyond 2-3x, and manufacturing EBITDA per ton, and it repeatedly said it could not give forecasts.

Pithampur Italian press ramp-up (currently ~25% ramp, targeting 35%/50%/75%; significant contribution by mid-FY28)

growth.why: Management guides flattish volumes and manufacturing revenue for FY27 with ramp-up only toward end FY27/start FY28, export share down to ~45% and freight/Middle East disruption weighing, while Q1 capex was under INR5 crore and most of the Dewas spend is deferred to H2 FY27.
